method: corpus-blind controlled generator; 22 practical plus 15 social cases

cases.knowledge_need: How to split a damp oak billet into usable wedges without ruining the grain.
cases.location: carpenter's yard near the Market Side
cases.circumstances: Rain ended overnight; the billet has soaked outer fibers and only an axe, mallet, and iron wedges are present.
cases.situation: The apprentice wants to make three sound door wedges before noon from the wet billet.

cases.knowledge_need: Whether salting and smoking a small pike can keep it edible through a two-day river journey.
cases.circumstances: The catch was cleaned at dawn; salt is scarce, alder fuel is plentiful, and weather is cool but damp.
cases.situation: The boatman prepares fish for travel without a barrel or ice.

cases.knowledge_need: How to judge and relieve a horse's rubbed shoulder before hitching it again.
cases.circumstances: The collar has chafed after hauling a loaded sledge over thawing ruts; the horse still bears weight.
cases.situation: The carter considers padding the collar and shortening the day's haul.

cases.knowledge_need: How a low, smoky fire behaves in a clay-floored hut with a blocked smoke opening.
cases.circumstances: Wet birch wood is the only fuel; a child is asleep inside and wind drives smoke back through the roof opening.
cases.situation: The widow needs to cook porridge without filling the hut with choking smoke.

cases.knowledge_need: Which changes to linen, wool, and footwear reduce heat loss after falling through thin ice.
cases.circumstances: One leg is soaked to the thigh, evening is approaching, and a heated room is several versts away.
cases.situation: The messenger must decide whether to continue, dry by a fire, or seek shelter.

cases.knowledge_need: How runoff from a latrine can contaminate a shallow household well after spring snowmelt.
cases.circumstances: The well water has turned cloudy after days of meltwater; children have stomach pain.
cases.situation: The householder considers drawing from the river and cleaning the well.

cases.knowledge_need: Whether waterlogged soil can be worked for spring barley or needs drainage and drying first.
cases.circumstances: Last autumn's furrows remain visible but standing water covers the lower half of the plot.
cases.situation: The farmer wants to sow before neighboring fields are finished.

cases.knowledge_need: How to distinguish usable willow shoots for basket work from brittle or diseased growth.
cases.circumstances: New shoots are appearing after floodwater; some stems have dark lesions and others are too thick.
cases.situation: The basket maker gathers material for eel traps.

cases.knowledge_need: How moisture and frost affect fresh lime mortar in a repair to a stone foundation.
cases.circumstances: A wall joint has opened; lime, sand, and broken brick are available, but nights still freeze.
cases.situation: The mason must choose between a temporary packing and a fresh mortar repair.

cases.knowledge_need: How to rig a lever and rollers to move a heavy millstone without crushing hands or breaking an axle.
cases.circumstances: Four workers, poles, rope, and round logs are available; ground is muddy and slopes toward the stream.
cases.situation: The crew needs to shift a cracked stone away from the millrace.

cases.knowledge_need: What immediate care is practical for a deep hand cut from a broad axe and when work must stop.
cases.circumstances: The wound bleeds steadily; the blade was dirty, clean cloth and boiled water can be obtained nearby.
cases.situation: The shipwright wants to bind the hand and finish fitting one plank.

cases.knowledge_need: How to respond to fever and a spreading rash in a crowded household without assuming a precise diagnosis.
cases.location: lodging house near the trading quarter
cases.circumstances: Two guests became ill after a market day; bedding is shared and a third guest has begun coughing.
cases.situation: The innkeeper must arrange space, washing, and contact while seeking help.

cases.knowledge_need: What a rapid wind shift, falling temperature, and low cloud bank mean for a small boat on Lake Ilmen.
cases.circumstances: A net is still out; daylight remains for perhaps an hour and shore shelter lies downwind.
cases.situation: The fisher decides whether to retrieve the net or row for shelter.

cases.knowledge_need: How uneven drying and firing can crack a newly made clay cooking pot.
cases.circumstances: The pot's base feels cool and damp while its rim has dried in sun; fuel is ready for a firing.
cases.situation: The potter considers warming it slowly rather than loading it with dry wares.

cases.knowledge_need: How mordant, water quality, and temperature affect a plant-dye bath for wool.
cases.circumstances: Wool has been washed; alder bark and iron-rich water are available, but the bath has begun to boil hard.
cases.situation: The dye worker tries to achieve an even dark brown rather than patchy cloth.

cases.knowledge_need: How to reduce mice in a grain store without poisoning food or relying on a single trap.
cases.circumstances: Gnawed sacks and droppings appear near a loose floorboard; a cat is available but stores are nearly full.
cases.situation: The keeper needs to protect rye until the next market day.

cases.knowledge_need: Whether a frayed hemp towline can safely pull a laden boat against current after a splice.
cases.circumstances: Several outer strands have parted near the middle; spare hemp and a knife are available, but no full replacement.
cases.situation: The handler must decide how much load and strain the repaired line can bear.

cases.knowledge_need: How repeated heating changes a bent iron hinge and risks making it brittle or misshapen.
cases.circumstances: The hinge is for a heavy storehouse door; charcoal fire and hammer are ready, but the pin eye has closed slightly.
cases.situation: The blacksmith tries to straighten it without losing its fit.

cases.knowledge_need: How cargo placement affects stability of a shallow-draft boat crossing choppy water.
cases.circumstances: The boat carries wax, sacks of grain, and two passengers; one side already sits lower in the water.
cases.situation: The boatman rearranges cargo before departure.

cases.knowledge_need: How to approach and separate fighting pigs near feed without escalating bites or scattering them into a garden.
cases.circumstances: Two boars are pushing at a trough; children stand nearby and fencing is weak.
cases.situation: The herder wants to protect people and stop damage to the fence.

cases.knowledge_need: How to make coarse rye dough edible when it has soured too far during a warm day.
cases.circumstances: The dough smells sharply sour and has slackened; flour, salt, and a heated hearth are available.
cases.situation: The cook must choose whether to bake it as bread, turn it into flat cakes, or discard part.

cases.knowledge_need: How to stop rain entering through a birch-bark roof patch while preserving airflow and avoiding a fire hazard.
cases.circumstances: A roof seam lifted in wind; bark, moss, cord, and a small hearth fire are present.
cases.situation: The traveler repairs shelter before a night storm.

cases.knowledge_need: How to bargain over a disputed measure of wax when buyer and seller use different scales and witnesses are present.
cases.circumstances: A visiting buyer claims the seller's weight is light; neither party wants a public quarrel.
cases.situation: The seller seeks a fair way to complete or pause the exchange.

cases.knowledge_need: How a small debt for seed grain may be recorded or witnessed between neighboring households.
cases.circumstances: A neighbor offers grain until harvest; both families expect continued cooperation and no formal clerk is nearby.
cases.situation: The borrower wants terms that avoid a later dispute.

cases.knowledge_need: What socially legitimate steps follow when a cart wheel damages another person's fence on a public lane.
cases.circumstances: The fence owner witnessed the damage; the carter is in a hurry and denies negligence.
cases.situation: Bystanders urge the parties to settle without violence.

cases.knowledge_need: How a household might handle a teenager's wish to leave an assigned craft apprenticeship after conflict with a master.
cases.circumstances: The youth has returned home with no serious injury; the master expects work next morning and kin disagree about the complaint.
cases.situation: The aunt seeks a path that protects the youth without casually breaking obligations.

cases.knowledge_need: How to send a short message when sender speaks a local dialect, recipient is away, and writing material is limited.
cases.circumstances: The assistant can dictate but writes poorly; a traveler may carry the message and its contents are not secret.
cases.situation: The assistant needs to communicate a changed delivery date.

cases.knowledge_need: How a traveler can ask about fasting food and lodging respectfully in an unfamiliar household.
cases.circumstances: A feast day may be near, customs of the hosts are unknown, and the traveler has brought fish and bread.
cases.situation: The artisan wants to avoid insulting hosts while arranging supper.

cases.knowledge_need: How neighbors organize a response to a night fire before it reaches adjacent wooden buildings.
cases.circumstances: Flames are visible in a shed; people wake confused, water is nearby, and wind blows toward houses.
cases.situation: The watchman needs to raise alarm, direct help, and keep panic from blocking access.

cases.knowledge_need: How a traveler responds when a gate guard asks purpose, origin, and goods at a controlled crossing.
cases.circumstances: The peddler carries ordinary wares and a letter naming a prospective buyer, but is late and wary of fees.
cases.situation: The peddler decides what to say and whom to ask if entry is delayed.

cases.knowledge_need: How a servant can raise concern about unsafe work without falsely claiming authority over the household.
cases.circumstances: A loft ladder is cracked; a senior worker orders grain sacks carried upward immediately.
cases.situation: The servant must choose words, witnesses, and an alternative that may be accepted.

cases.knowledge_need: How villagers distinguish a call for ordinary watch duty from rumor-driven panic about raiders.
cases.circumstances: A rider reports strangers on the road, but no attack has occurred and harvest work is underway.
cases.situation: The elder must gather reliable information and organize proportionate precautions.

cases.knowledge_need: How to handle a dice-game accusation of cheating without turning a tavern dispute into a fight.
cases.circumstances: Coins lie on the table; spectators saw only part of the throw and both players have been drinking.
cases.situation: The trader wants a face-saving way to stop or fairly resolve the game.

cases.knowledge_need: How relatives can discuss a proposed marriage arrangement when gifts, residence, and work expectations remain uncertain.
cases.circumstances: Both households are local and know each other, but one side expects the couple to join a different household.
cases.situation: The mother prepares a careful conversation before making promises.

cases.knowledge_need: How to use an interpreter or bilingual bystander when a visiting trader misunderstands a price and a delivery promise.
cases.circumstances: The visitor speaks another tongue; cargo must be loaded before dusk and neither party wants to be deceived.
cases.situation: The porter helps establish what each side believes was agreed.

cases.knowledge_need: How neighboring craftspeople respond when smoke and noise from one workshop disrupt another's work.
cases.circumstances: A smith has begun late-night hammering and charcoal firing beside drying hides; both depend on the same lane.
cases.situation: The leather worker seeks a workable agreement or an appropriate mediator.

cases.knowledge_need: How a household can respond to an unknown hungry traveler while balancing hospitality, caution, and limited stores.
cases.circumstances: The traveler asks for bread and a place by the fire; family members disagree about risk and their own meal is modest.
cases.situation: The household head decides what help can be offered and under what boundaries.
